media.alt: Senator Jamiluddin Aali lauds AKU's role in national integration

content.text: "The Aga Khan University draws its faculty, staff and students from all the four provinces which is an excellent example of national integration," said Chief Guest Senator Jamiluddin Aali at the Independence Day celebrations at The Aga Khan University (AKU) campus. Commenting on the great natural advantages with which Allah has blessed the nation, Senator Aali said "Seventeen countries of the world have no access to the sea; eleven countries do not have rivers. While eighty-two countries do not produce sugar, rice or wheat and seventy-eight grow no cotton. With its immense resources Pakistan has all the potential to become the great nation Quaid-e-Azam envisioned. "

After the impressive flag hoisting ceremony by Dr Shamsh Kassim-Lakha, President of AKU, the Senator and poet delighted the audience with a memorable rendering of the popular patriotic song he has authored - "Jeevay, Jeevay Pakistan." He urged the faculty, staff and their families to treasure Urdu as the language chosen by the Quaid-e-Azam as the national language of Pakistan. Spoken and understood in all four provinces, it is the language that can promote national integration.

"The people of Pakistan are indebted to the generosity of the Aga Khan for this excellent centre of higher learning," said Senator Jamiluddin Aali. Under the direction and vision of the University's founder and Chancellor the Aga Khan, he said The Aga Khan University is both a repository of advanced knowledge and a training ground for future generations of the country.

Senator Jamiluddin Aali also highlighted the contributions made by Sir Sultan Mohamed Shah, Aga Khan III, to the Pakistan Movement. He stressed the important role the Aga Khan played in the establishment of the Aligarh Muslim University for the Muslims of India. Building on that tradition, his grandson, His Highness Prince Karim Aga Khan has paved the way for academic excellence by establishing The Aga Khan University in the city of his grandfather's birth.
